source_claims.label: Time travel is structurally impossible
source_claims.statement: No character can solve history by traveling backward into it. Starsilk permits reality editing and recursive action loops, not a conventional route into the past.

source_claims.label: Starsilk is executable substrate
source_claims.statement: Starsilk is literal programmable cosmological matter. A Macro is a repeatable action-loop embedded into that substrate, not a metaphor for magic or a loose spell effect.

source_claims.label: Stellar centers are Starsilk-bearing
source_claims.statement: Starsilk runs through stellar centers. Star-core access is therefore both a physical operation and access to a universe-level execution medium.

source_claims.label: Stellar equilibrium depends on the filament
source_claims.statement: A star remains structurally stable while its Starsilk remains in place. Pulling or severing that filament removes the tension sustaining the star’s equilibrium.

source_claims.label: Extraction executes collapse immediately
source_claims.statement: Successful extraction from a star does not merely damage it. The star undergoes immediate gravitational collapse toward a black hole, destroying its system.

source_claims.label: A successful dive becomes a star knife
source_claims.statement: A star dive that successfully pulls Starsilk is functionally a star knife: an execution surface whose consequence is stellar collapse.

source_claims.label: Death is final even when data remains
source_claims.statement: The dead do not persist as an ongoing conscious afterlife. Stars and Starsilk may preserve data, residue, archive traces, or structural memory without preserving continuing subjective suffering.

source_claims.label: Syrin blood is a dead-switch
source_claims.statement: Syrin blood contains a biological glitch that renders Starsilk inert. It therefore disables the same programmable substrate through which divine and Macro authority normally operates.

source_claims.label: Safe Starsilk contact is exceptionally rare
source_claims.statement: The known safe interaction routes are Tiger’s native immunity, the Syrin blood glitch, and Codec ’s Syrin-blood vapor method. Ordinary direct extraction remains catastrophic.

source_claims.label: Tiger made Starsilk deliberately
source_claims.statement: Starsilk is not a naturally discovered miracle. Tiger created it from the beginning as a betrayal instrument inside the divine order.

source_claims.label: Wordstreamer is murdered with Starsilk
source_claims.statement: Tiger uses the substrate he created to murder Wordstreamer, turning the universe’s executable medium into the mechanism of foundational divine betrayal.

source_claims.label: The first Starsilk bleed follows deletion
source_claims.statement: Wordstreamer’s deletion produces the first recorded Starsilk bleed: radiant azure thread appearing where memory refuses a clean overwrite.

source_claims.label: Aureal Gate is the Year 170 breaking point
source_claims.statement: The final war phase reaches the Aureal Gate in Year 170, when the Drakken use Starsilk as a weapon against divine architecture.

source_claims.label: Drakken Starsilk use proves Tiger can be hurt
source_claims.statement: The strategic shock is not merely another weapon. Mortal terraforming entities have discovered a substrate capable of injuring what divine hierarchy treated as structurally untouchable.

source_claims.label: Tiger commands Hal’Ven from Lacrimosa
source_claims.statement: Tiger is physically present in frontline command aboard the flagship Lacrimosa when he answers the Starsilk threat with heliocide.

source_claims.label: Codec’s WorldsVault breach uses Syrin-blood vapor
source_claims.statement: Codec employs the Syrin-blood vapor interaction method to bypass Starsilk-based defenses during the breach, weaponizing the same biological glitch Tiger tried to erase.

source_claims.label: Inert Starsilk is the Partition’s constitutional physics
source_claims.statement: Within the Partition, Starsilk cannot function as active divine or administrative code. The substrate remains part of reality while its old domination permissions are disabled.

source_claims.label: Codec removes himself from the world he creates
source_claims.statement: Codec repairs Kail’s mouth with old-universe data and sends him across. Because Codec’s own nervous system depends on active Starsilk, he decompiles in the between-space and purges his footprint rather than becoming the Partition’s new sovereign.

source_claims.domain: Post-Wall Drakken / civilization beyond the Wall
source_claims.label: Codec crosses the Wall seeking Starsilk knowledge
source_claims.statement: Codec expects danger and imagines he may need to coerce knowledge from a lone surviving Titan. Discovering a living civilization destroys that premise: he can ask living people rather than extract answers from a remnant.
